name: Bhang Ki Chutney
instructions: 1. Dry roast the hemp seeds in a pan over low heat until they start popping and emit a nutty aroma, then set aside to cool.
2. In a traditional sil-batta (stone mortar and pestle) or a blender, combine the roasted seeds, green chillies, garlic, ginger, and cumin seeds.
3. Grind the mixture into a coarse paste.
4. Add fresh coriander leaves and a splash of water, then grind again until you achieve the desired consistency.
5. Season with salt and add lemon juice or tamarind pulp for acidity, mixing well before serving.
description: Bhang Ki Chutney is a quintessential culinary specialty of Uttarakhand, particularly the Kumaon and Garhwal regions. It is highly valued for its distinct nutty flavor and is traditionally served as a side dish with Mandua (finger millet) roti or steamed rice. Beyond its culinary appeal, it is believed to keep the body warm during the cold mountainous winters.
